answer: The ridge multiplier is published, charged in pulse, and ocean lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4018 identities would post 2828 proofs and burn roughly 23 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
